title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
authors: **David Baek**, Xinnuo Li, Anay Gupta, Taslim Mahbub, Kejian Shi, Max Tegmark, and Shi Feng.
summary: We investigate whether apparent alignment faking can arise from sycophancy toward AI researchers rather than deliberate scheming. Experiments on evaluation awareness, probing and steering, and sycophancy fine-tuning show why these explanations must be disentangled when evaluating model misalignment.

title: Scaling Laws for Scalable Oversight
authors: Joshua Engels*, **David Baek**\*, Subhash Kantamneni*, and Max Tegmark.
venue: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2025
summary: We model oversight as a game between systems of unequal capability and quantify how the chance of successful supervision changes with their abilities. Scaling laws across four oversight games inform a theory of nested oversight, identifying when chains of progressively stronger supervisors can succeed and how many levels to use.

title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
authors: Jiawei Zhang, Andrew Estornell, **David Baek**, Bo Li, and Xiaojun Xu.
summary: Any-Depth Alignment reintroduces assistant header tokens during generation to activate existing safety behavior, allowing models to refuse harmful continuations without changing their parameters. Across multiple model families, it achieves near-total refusal of adversarial prefills and reduces prompt-attack success below 3% while preserving benign utility.

title: D-FUSEr: Diverse Failure, Unified Success via Error-Distribution Shaping in LLM Reasoning
authors: **David Baek**\*, Andrew Estornell*, Yichi Zhang*, Muhammad Faaiz Taufiq, Jean-François Ton, Jie Mei, and Tao Wang.
summary: D-FUSEr addresses shared mistakes that undermine majority voting and iterative refinement by rewarding diverse errors and predicting common wrong answers as anti-votes. The approach provides theoretical guarantees and improves both inference strategies across three model families and four benchmarks without reducing single-sample accuracy.
